in_text_mentions: Plain radiographs (X-rays) can show the characteristic multiple loose bodies, particularly after they have calcified or ossified (Figure 1). However, in the early stages of the disease, the cartilaginous nodules might not be calcified, with a normal image at X-rays [23]. Calcified nodules within the joint space will be visible on X-rays. These calcifications frequently exhibit a chondroid mineralization pattern that reflects the mineralization of cartilage tissue [24].

On haematoxylin and eosin at 50× of magnification, multiple cartilaginous nodules variably cellular with peripheral ossification are observed (A); at 200× of magnification clustered chondrocytes in a hyaline matrix without significant cytological atypia are evident (B).
in_text_mentions: Microscopically, the nodules consist of lobules of hyaline cartilage with increased cellularity and clustered chondrocytes embedded in a chondroid matrix; mild cytological atypia, binucleated chondrocytes, and focal calcification or endochondral ossification may be observed without implying malignancy [9,24,29] (Figure 4). Residual synovial lining tissue often occurs around the cartilage fragments.

in_text_mentions: on this systematic review of reported cases, objective diagnostic findings for SChS include medullary bone invasion on imaging or histology and pathologic findings consistent with grade II or III chondrosarcoma [30, 33, 34] (Fig. 2). Concerning features include rapid clinical progression of pain, local recurrence within 12 mos after resection, soft tissue infiltration of tumor, and large size [34] (Fig. 3). Similar to the diagnostic and grading challenges of other chondroid malignancies, accurate assessment of SChS requires consideration of clinical, radiographic and histologic findings [32].

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 2 panels (A, B). A: Axial unenhanced thin-slice CT in a published case report of synovial chondromatosis of the hip. The arrowhead marks a homogenous soft tissue-isodense mass filling the right femoroacetabular joint space (non-calcified chondroid synovial mass), with slight acetabular fossa erosion per in-text; real human-patient image clearly attributable to the configured target disease. B: Coronal CT reformat from the same case report of synovial chondromatosis of the hip, displaying the same soft tissue-isodense mass occupying the right femoroacetabular joint space (arrowhead) with joint space widening relative to the contralateral side; a real human-patient image of the target disease, consistent with a non-calcified (variant) presentation.

panels.rationale: Single plain radiograph (panel A; the figure as supplied is one radiograph even though the caption also references MRI). The disease-focused article title ('disseminated synovial chondromatosis: a case report') plus the captioned/in-text manifestation support attribution: multiple soft-tissue calcifications within and outside the joint capsule, with the in-text specifying 'multiple intra-articular calcific and ossific loose bodies' and 'large calcified bursal extensions,' matching the calcified intra-articular loose-bodies finding. The plain-film appearance had prompted an impression of idiopathic tumoral calcinosis, but the article diagnosis and prior triage keep the figure under synovial chondromatosis and no caption text names another disease as the panel's diagnosis; it is a real patient image of readable quality and not third-party. The prominent extra-articular calcified masses are proposed because the vocabulary key is intra-articular only. The rare disseminated/extra-articular extent is a recognized less-common (variant) presentation; the caption does not call it atypical. Age/ethnicity are not stated in the provided caption or in-text.
